test-case.name: BareFormReachableOnlyByOmittingAnOptional_Warns
test-case.output: [VoxrCommandParser] Intent 'fire' has the pattern "fire {?quantity} {weapon} (with its optional elements omitted)" and the longer "fire {weapon} at {target}", which extends it with the required literal "at" in front of slot "{target}". If that literal is dropped, the longer pattern loses that element's credit while the bare one still matches perfectly. The bare one is now charged for the words it leaves unexplained (issue #65 §5.2), so it usually loses that exchange — but not when the stranded value's first word could itself begin some pattern, which stops the charge and hands the bare form the win with the value the speaker did say discarded silently. Make the literal optional ("?at") to close the case that remains: an otherwise-complete match then reaches the same score with or without the word and wins on consumed span. That trade is not free: an optional literal also lowers the score of matches that are already missing something, and stops anchoring the slot behind it, which can then claim adjacent tokens.

test-case.name: SiblingWarning_LeavesTheDroppableLiteralWarningAlone
test-case.output: [VoxrCommandParser] Intent 'decelerate' has the pattern "decelerate" and the longer "decelerate by {burn_level}", which extends it with the required literal "by" in front of slot "{burn_level}". If that literal is dropped, the longer pattern loses that element's credit while the bare one still matches perfectly. The bare one is now charged for the words it leaves unexplained (issue #65 §5.2), so it usually loses that exchange — but not when the stranded value's first word could itself begin some pattern, which stops the charge and hands the bare form the win with the value the speaker did say discarded silently. Make the literal optional ("?by") to close the case that remains: an otherwise-complete match then reaches the same score with or without the word and wins on consumed span. That trade is not free: an optional literal also lowers the score of matches that are already missing something, and stops anchoring the slot behind it, which can then claim adjacent tokens.

test-case.name: EagerFlush_PrefixCommand_WaitsForTheWindow
test-case.output: [VoxrCommandParser] Pattern "status" (intent 'status') is a bare form of "status report {target}" (intent 'status_report'), which extends it with the required literal "report" in front of slot "{target}". If that literal is dropped, the longer pattern loses that element's credit while the bare one still matches perfectly. The bare one is now charged for the words it leaves unexplained (issue #65 §5.2), so it usually loses that exchange — but not when the stranded value's first word could itself begin some pattern, which stops the charge and hands the bare form the win with the value the speaker did say discarded silently. Make the literal optional ("?report") to close the case that remains: an otherwise-complete match then reaches the same score with or without the word and wins on consumed span. That trade is not free: an optional literal also lowers the score of matches that are already missing something, and stops anchoring the slot behind it, which can then claim adjacent tokens.

test-case.name: SecondInitialise_RejectedLoudly_OwnerKeepsBridge
test-case.output: InitialiseAsync: another VoxrSpeechRecogniser (on GameObject 'OwnerRecogniser') already owns the recogniser. VoXR supports one active recogniser per process. On device the bridge is file-scope native state with no per-instance handle, so a second instance would inherit the first's model path, sample rate and gain, and free its recognizer on destroy; the Windows Editor backend is per-instance and could have coexisted, but is held to the same rule so a scene that works here cannot fail on device. Call ReleaseNativeResources() on the existing recogniser first — that frees the claim synchronously, whereas Object.Destroy only frees it at the end of the frame.
